newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: China plans major air fleet expansion by 2000.
newsitem.headline: China plans major air fleet expansion by 2000.

text.p: China expects to have an air fleet of more than 1,000 commercial aircraft by 2000 and plans orders of as many as 300 new planes in coming years, a senior official of China's Civil Aviation Administration (CAAC) said on Friday.

Hai Liancheng, CAAC's director general of finance, told an international civil aviation conference in Geneva the expansion was expected under China's development plan for 1996-2000 but did not say what type of planes China planned to order.
"We plan to order more than 300 planes. We plan to increase our orders," he said.
Liancheng did not say whether these would be firm orders or involve options. He also did not say how China planned to finance this expansion.
As of end-1996, China had a total 317 aircraft leased from countries including the United States, Germany, France, Japan, Sweden and Hong Kong at a cost of $11.8 billion, Liancheng said.
China's total air fleet now had 443 aircraft, including the leases, worth a total of $16 billion, he said.
"By the year 2000, the number of aircraft in the entire industry will reach 1,000 and more," he said.
